manufacturer.olivetti.description: Italian manufacturer whose personal computers combined original engineering, industrial design and several families of IBM-compatible systems.
family.olivetti-pcs.description: The Olivetti PCS family covers compact late-1980s and early-1990s personal computers built around the V30, 80286 and 80386SX generations. BluMach keeps the commercial family together while preserving the distinct hardware of every model.
product.olivetti-pcs86.summary: Compact V30 computer with integrated VGA and unusual PS/2-style peripherals.
product.olivetti-pcs86.history: The PCS86 is a late XT-class design that combines a NEC V30 processor with integrated VGA, an XTA hard disk interface and two PS/2-style peripheral ports. Resident Diagnostics 1.09 and an MS-DOS floppy boot have been reproduced in the research build.
product.olivetti-pcs286.summary: Twelve-megahertz 80286 model with integrated VGA and IDE storage.
product.olivetti-pcs286.history: The PCS 286 was the middle member of the PCS line. Preserved firmware identifies BIOS and Resident Diagnostics revisions 1.37 and 1.42. The machine boots MS-DOS in the research build, while exact keyboard timing, onboard video and CMOS behavior still require refinement.
product.olivetti-pcs286s.summary: 12 MHz TI/OLIMCU16 board with preserved Olivetti BIOS 2.06 and certified emulation with documented limits.
product.olivetti-pcs286s.history: BIOS 2.06 offers 12/12, 12/6 and 6/6 MHz modes. The 2021 preservation thread proposed that this TI/OLIMCU16 may have been a PCS 286 service-replacement board or a revision used in some PCS 286S systems. BluMach preserves that hypothesis without identifying it as the commercial 16 MHz PCS 286S.
product.olivetti-pcs286s.warning: CERTIFIED with documented limits as a 12 MHz TI PCS 286/S: BIOS 2.06, POST, video, keyboard, RTC, 40 MB IDE and 1/2/4 MB memory are validated. Its exact identity as a replacement board or 286S revision remains open; EMS is pending.
product.olivetti-pcs286s16.summary: Documented commercial 16 MHz PCS 286S, not yet emulatable because its correct BIOS is missing.
product.olivetti-pcs286s16.history: Olivetti's 1991 brochure confirms a zero-wait-state 16 MHz 80286, 1 MB standard, up to 8 MB on-board, 16 MB system memory and 40, 80 and 120 MB disks. It is catalogued separately from the 12 MHz TI/OLIMCU16 board.
product.olivetti-pcs286s16.warning: EMULATION UNAVAILABLE: no verified BIOS for the commercial 16 MHz PCS 286S is preserved. TI/OLIMCU16 BIOS 2.06 is not reused because its clock modes correspond to 12 MHz.
product.ta-dario286s.summary: Possible Triumph-Adler counterpart of the 16 MHz 286S, preserved as a research lead.
product.ta-dario286s.history: The existence and exact identity of the Dario 286S require confirmation from primary documentation or physical hardware. It is catalogued separately to avoid confusing it with the 12 MHz Dario 286/P35 or assuming Olivetti firmware equivalence.
product.ta-dario286s.warning: EMULATION UNAVAILABLE: no verified Dario 286S BIOS is preserved and its exact relationship to the 16 MHz PCS 286S remains unconfirmed.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.summary: Sixteen-megahertz 80386SX model and the most advanced initial PCS machine.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.history: The PCS 386SX extends the family with a 16 MHz 80386SX, up to 8 MB of onboard memory and integrated Paradise VGA. Its recovered emulation remains experimental until the POST and chipset behavior are reproducible without provisional workarounds.
technical.ui.preparing: Technical documentation for this machine is still being prepared.
technical.ui.intro: This page separates documented hardware facts, behavior observed in original firmware, and the current fidelity of BluMach emulation.
technical.evidence.reverse_engineered: behavior recovered from BIOS code and testing
technical.evidence.implementation: current BluMach status; not necessarily a description of the original circuit
technical.evidence.observed: observed in preserved firmware and boot testing
technical.evidence.documented_and_modele: manufacturer manual compared with the BluMach implementation
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.cpu_bus: NEC V30 at 10 MHz with zero wait states, according to the September 1990 Olivetti brochure; 16-bit data bus with the 8-bit ISA expansion of its XT-class architecture.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.memory_: 640 KB conventional memory. Paired SIMM expansion provides 0, 384 or 1920 KB of EMS. Four 16 KB windows occupy 80000h–8FFFFh.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.video: Integrated Paradise VGA. The system BIOS also contains its initialization code, so a separate VGA option ROM at C0000h is not required.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.rom_lay: Two interleaved EPROMs, CSAB05 (even bytes) and CSAB04 (odd bytes), form 64 KB at F0000h–FFFFFh. The set contains system BIOS, VGA, XTA and diagnostics.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.bios_re: Resident Diagnostics Rev. 1.09. The preserved set passes its checksum and reaches the reset vector at FFFF0h.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.bios_id: For compatibility, INT 15h/C0h identifies the system as IBM PS/2 Model 30, submodel 109. This is a firmware choice, not the computer's commercial identity.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.diagnos: Tests CPU, ROM, DMA, PIC, timer, base and expanded memory, clock/calendar, printer, communications, drives and keyboard. The observed screen is revision 1.09.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.io_intr: The following addresses cover PCS86-specific board logic in addition to the usual compatible blocks.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.board_c: 60h–6Fh: keyboard, PIT/speaker and proprietary logic. Port 65h: bit 0 XTA, bit 1 LPT, bit 2 VGA, bit 4 COM1 and bit 7 startup/test latch according to the analyzed BIOS code.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.keyboar: Port 60h receives keyboard scan codes and IRQ1. Ports 66h–6Ah implement the board's dual PS/2-style peripheral interface; observed IDs are AB83h for the keyboard and 00h for the mouse.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.rtc: E0h–EFh: MM58167 and associated NVRAM. Commands B0h–B7h manage access and status; BIOS stores date, time and checksum in its own format.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.floppy: Compatible controller at 3F0h–3F7h. The physical bank selects 360 KB, 720 KB, 1.2 MB or 1.44 MB per drive with active-low combinations.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.hard_di: XTA interface at 320h–323h, IRQ5 and DMA3. The historical 20 MB configuration is a Conner CP3026 (615 cylinders, 4 heads, 17 sectors).
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.serial_: COM1 at 3F8h on IRQ4; the real diagnostics report two communications channels, while BluMach currently models the confirmed port. LPT1 is at 378h–37Fh, including special 37Ah behavior used by resident tests.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.video_p: Compatible VGA registers at 3C0h–3DFh and A0000h–BFFFFh video memory. Integrated-video selection goes through board control and VGA enable logic.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.ems: Page registers at 8400h–8403h; each selects the page for one of four 16 KB windows at 80000h–8FFFFh.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.jumpers: Active-low port 100h: bits 0–1 drive 0 type; bits 2–3 drive 1 type; bit 7 indicates an XTA disk. Per-drive codes are 00=360 KB, 10=1.2 MB, 01=720 KB, 11=1.44 MB. Bits 4–6 are not exposed as user options because the analyzed BIOS does not consume them.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.key_loc: The key/keyboard-lock state is reflected in bit 2 of port 66h.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.gui_beh: Automatic mode derives jumpers from installed drives. Manual mode can reproduce an exact physical bank, including inconsistent settings, for research and preservation.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.verifie: BIOS and MS-DOS boot; CPU, ROM, DMA, PIC, timer, 640 KB base memory, clock/calendar, printer, keyboard and EMS diagnostics. FDISK has also been tested with a 20 MB XTA disk.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.limitat: Electrical timing of the dual keyboard/mouse interface and some video-arbitration details remain functional approximations. Mapping the reported second communications channel still needs physical evidence.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.source_: Olivetti PCS86 technical notes by John Elliott
CSAB04/CSAB05 EPROMs, Resident Diagnostics 1.09, Customer Test and execution observations made during recovery.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.brochur: PCS 86, Olivetti Office Italia product sheet dated September 1990, 2 pages
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.cpu_bu: Intel 80286 at 12 MHz; AT-class platform with optional 80287 coprocessor.
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.memory: Documented 1 to 4 MB configurations; BIOS tests base and extended memory during POST.
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.storag: Integrated IDE/ATA. Preserved configurations include the 20 MB Conner CP3022 and 40 MB CP346.
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.chipse: G2 GC101A + GC102 set, later incorporated into the Headland family. BluMach uses 86Box's GC101/102/103 device plus Olivetti-specific IOC02 logic.
GC101 combines peripheral control, timing, arbitration and memory control; GC102 supplies address/data buffers and parity. The design supports up to 4 MB, matching the PCS 286 commercial limit.
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.headla: The current model exposes 1ECh as EMS data, 1EDh as configuration index, 1EEh as EMS map index and 1EFh as configuration data. This is BluMach's functional interface and is not yet claimed as a complete physical decode of the motherboard.
GC101/GC102 Data Sheet, 55 pages, preserved inside BluMach
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.bios_r: Sets 1.37 (one archival file was labelled 1.34) and 1.42. The 16 MHz PCS 286 S variant remains separate and is not presented as identical hardware.
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.setup: BIOS Extended Setup stores floppy, drive geometry/type, memory and board options in CMOS.
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.diagno: The observed Customer Test validates DMA controllers, keyboard, clock/calendar, protected mode and CMOS, and reports floppy, fixed-disk and configuration errors.
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.rom_la: 128 KB BIOS at E0000h–FFFFFh. Revision 1.42 comes from two 64 KB 27C512 EPROMs, LOW and HIGH, byte-interleaved. The older set identifies itself as 1.37 although its archival label said 1.34.
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.memory: Test 6 writes RAM-REMAPPING at 60000h and requires it to be readable at 80000h. This exposed a 128 KB alias controlled by memory logic; BluMach reproduces it explicitly while the chipset control effect is completed.
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.ioc02: Ports 68h, 6Ah and 6Ch. Phoenix 1.42 expects the first 6Ah read to publish 04h (subsystem ready). The device also resets on warm reset so stale values cannot cause I/O CONTROLLER ERROR 2.
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.keyboa: Routine at F000:D192. It sends FFh to the keyboard, receives FAh as ACK and then waits for AAh as BAT result. Keyboard Error 4 means exactly that FAh arrived but BAT did not finish before timeout; this finding allowed the sequence to be fixed without fabricating keystrokes.
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.cmos_b: Phoenix compares the BDA equipment word at 0040:0010 with CMOS 14h. For 80x25, one floppy and no coprocessor the base value is 0020h. CMOS 0Eh holds diagnostic state and 10h the floppy type; checksum covers 10h–2Dh and is stored at 2Eh/2Fh.
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.video_: No valid 55 AAh option-ROM signature appears at C0000h. Historical halves named Video at E0000 and BIOS at F0000 are actually parts of system BIOS 1.37. Paradise/Olivetti initialization is integrated in the main ROM.
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.verifi: BIOS 1.42, POST, Extended Setup, MS-DOS boot and Customer Test execution with a 40 MB IDE disk.
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.limita: The complete physical I/O decode, exact effect of some GC101A registers and authentic internal M5L8042-243P ROM remain to be documented. A functional approximation is used where no dump or schematic is available.
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.firmwa: BIOS 1.37 and 1.42, Resident Diagnostics, Customer Test and POST traces. Original EPROMs, normalized images and CMOS states are kept separately.
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.progra: PAL16L8 2P04 and 3P01 are preserved as JEDEC. The documented physical controller is a Mitsubishi M5L8042-243P; its authentic internal ROM has not been recovered. 62410C62.BIN is not that ROM and is not loaded into the 8042.
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.brochu: PCS 286, Olivetti Office Italia product sheet dated October 1989, 2 pages
product.olivetti-pcs286s.technical.cpu_b: Intel 80286 at 12 MHz; BIOS modes 12/12, 12/6 and 6/6 MHz; socket for an optional 80287 coprocessor.
product.olivetti-pcs286s.technical.memor: 1, 2 and 4 MB are validated on the TI/OLIMCU16 board. Total 8 and 16 MB profiles also boot using a hypothetical generic ISA/AT card providing 4 or 12 MB from the 4 MB address. These profiles prove technical feasibility, not the existence of a specific Olivetti card.
product.olivetti-pcs286s.technical.stora: The brochure offers one 1.44 MB floppy and 40, 80 or 120 MB hard disks. BIOS 2.06 has now been validated booting a 40 MB CP346 (805 cylinders, 4 heads, 26 sectors); 80 and 120 MB remain pending.
product.olivetti-pcs286s.technical.bios_: Olivetti BIOS and Resident Diagnostics 2.06 dated 20 May 1991. Two 64 KiB EPROMs exactly reconstruct the 128 KiB FULL image; Setup supports English, Italian, German, French and Spanish.
product.olivetti-pcs286s.technical.video: The integrated Paradise VGA is now initialized by BIOS 2.06 and renders Resident Diagnostics and Extended Setup correctly; no external video ROM is required.
product.olivetti-pcs286s.technical.frequ: Extended Setup offers 12/12, 12/6 and 6/6 MHz, so BluMach catalogues and runs this board at 12 MHz. This supports the community hypothesis of a TI service board or shared revision without turning it into the commercial 16 MHz PCS 286S; F7 remains unmodeled.
product.olivetti-pcs286s.technical.olimc: BIOS 2.06 probes 0208h, 0218h, 0258h, 0268h, 02A8h, 02B8h and 02E8h. It initially uses 0208h while sizing RAM, then relocates the interface to 0218h, with four 16 KB windows at base+0000h/+4000h/+8000h/+C000h. BluMach now reproduces this renegotiation and the observed aliases; the exact TACT82300/OLIMCU16 division remains unresolved.
product.olivetti-pcs286s.technical.verif: Machine certified with documented limits: BIOS 2.06, POST, integrated Paradise VGA, RTC, keyboard—including the MS-DOS F3-reset-F2 sequence—40 MB CP346 boot and 1/2/4 MB board memory. Its identity is presented as a 12 MHz TI PCS 286/S; 8/16 MB totals use hypothetical ISA/AT expansion.
product.olivetti-pcs286s.technical.limit: EMS remains pending: HIMEM.SYS can manage XMS on the 80286, but EMM386 cannot run on a 286 and no OLIMCU- or Olivetti-card-specific EMS driver is preserved. Shadow and F7/clock switching are still incomplete. The 8/16 MB ISA profiles do not reproduce an identified historical card.
product.olivetti-pcs286s.technical.broch: PCS 286 S, Italian Olivetti brochure dated June 1991, 2 pages
product.olivetti-pcs286s.technical.board: 2021 preservation thread with high-resolution photographs and confirmation of multiple PCS 286 boards, including TI TACT82300 + OLIMCU16.
product.olivetti-pcs286s.technical.credi: Thanks to the participants in the 2021 it.comp.retrocomputing thread, who documented the different boards and preserved the physical TI/OLIMCU16 evidence, and to EngiNerd89/Murdock for the Olivetti-PCS and Olivetti-OLIMCU branches, ROM names, inventory and port leads. BluMach later contributes disassembly, 0208h→0218h negotiation and 640+384 KB validation; it does not claim the original discoveries or materials.
product.olivetti-pcs286s.technical.refer: Unfinished EngiNerd89/Murdock Olivetti-PCS branch identifying ROM 2.05/2.06, TACT8230x, OLIMCU16, PC87310 and Paradise VGA.
product.olivetti-pcs286s.technical.olimc: Historical Olivetti-OLIMCU branch, commit e1efcf6 (30 May 2021). It adds a provisional M290S using a NEAT substitute and explicitly records that OLIMCU16 EMS/shadow management is missing. Its comments note 0208h/0209h and 68h/6Ah, but it contains no OLIMCU implementation and is used only as a research lead.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.cpu_: Intel 80386SX at 16 MHz with a 16-bit external data bus; optional 80387SX remains pending physical confirmation.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.memo: 1 to 8 MB onboard; BIOS tests base and extended memory and stores configuration in 128-byte CMOS.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.vide: Integrated Paradise PVGA1A with 256 KB; OVC 1.06 video firmware is embedded in the known BIOS set.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.stor: Integrated IDE/ATA with documented 20, 40 and 100 MB configurations; the BluMach test machine uses 100 MB.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.chip: BluMach models the machine with a Headland HT18-B single-chip 80386SX controller, adding proprietary IOC02 logic and a functional PC87310 I/O block. The exact revision fitted to the Olivetti board still awaits physical confirmation.

The HT18 manual integrates CPU interface, clocks, ISA bus, I/O decode, keyboard and RTC interface, DMA, two PICs, timer, port 92h, coprocessor and DRAM/EMS/ROM control. This explains why much of the board behavior depends on one circuit.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.head: BluMach models 1ECh–1EFh for EMS maps and configuration registers, plus fast port 92h with Headland polarity. Registers control RAM mapping, shadow and EMS; the catalog distinguishes this interface from Olivetti ports 68h/6Ah/6Ch.
Headland HT18 80386SX Single Chip, revision 2 dated September 1991, 105 pages (user-supplied; reference for the functional model, not standalone proof of the board's exact population)
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.setu: Built-In Set-Up covers date/time, floppy, disk, video and other board options. Its fields depend on the firmware's own CMOS format.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.diag: Customer Test exercises memory, clock, controllers and peripherals. U_MGR from the preserved copy hangs and remains under investigation to distinguish disk damage from an emulation incompatibility.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.rom_: Two 64 KB LOW/HIGH images are byte-interleaved into 128 KB at E0000h–FFFFFh. The global eight-bit checksum is zero. The first 24 KB contain OVC 1.06.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.kbc_: At F000:37C6 (physical F37C6h), Phoenix sends AEh to the 8042, waits for OBF at 64h and requires 3Bh from 60h. The generic 8042 only enabled the keyboard and left BIOS waiting; BluMach queues one machine-specific 3Bh response.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.ioc0: Selector is at 68h, data/status at 6Ah, with an additional 6Ch register. Phoenix 1.14 verifies 55h/AAh writes and expects 6Ah reads to apply XOR 20h; with selector 00h a write must not latch. Warm reset restores 04h/04h/FFh.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.memo: HT18-B owns conventional memory, 384 KB relocation, shadow RAM and EMS. With CR0 bit 2 clear, the 384 KB hidden by the upper-memory area is relocated above 1 MB. BIOS 1.14 does not contain the PCS 286 RAM-REMAPPING 6000h/8000h test; that copied alias and the generic AT remap were removed because they overlapped the real HT18 maps.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.cmos: 128-byte Phoenix CMOS. An initial 1 MB configuration uses 640 KB base, 384 KB extended and equipment 21h/20h according to boot context; 80387SX presence updates its bit and requires the 10h–2Dh checksum to be recalculated.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.vide: OVC 1.06 is embedded in the system BIOS and controls the integrated 256 KB PVGA1A; therefore the device does not mount an external Paradise ROM at C0000h.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.veri: BIOS, Built-In Set-Up, MS-DOS boot, configured memory and a 100 MB IDE disk.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.limi: Emulation remains experimental. The full chipset map, some CMOS/POST behavior and the U_MGR hang remain unresolved. Diagnostic copies require caution because DOS/Barrotes_1310 was historically detected in U_MGR.EXE.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.firm: Phoenix BIOS 1.14, embedded OVC 1.06, disassembly of F000:37C6 and IOC02 paths, cold/warm boot traces and tests with/without an 80387SX.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.diag: Resident Diagnostics, Customer Utility 1.51 and Tutorial 2.2. Original IMDs preserve one unavailable sector; working RAW copies fill it with F6h. The sanitized Customer Utility copy remains separate from the original.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.broc: PCS 386 SX, Olivetti product sheet dated September 1990, 2 pages
manufacturer.triumph-adler.description: German office-machine and computer manufacturer whose Dario systems shared their engineering with Olivetti PCS models during the Olivetti ownership period.
manufacturer.triumph-adler.history: Founded in 1896, the company became Triumph-Adler and moved from typewriters and calculators into electronic computing. Its milestones include the TA 10 in 1971 and the Alphatronic family from 1979. Volkswagen sold its majority holding to Olivetti in 1986. TA subsequently manufactured closely related systems sold as Dario/P35/P45 and as Olivetti PCS machines. After restructuring in 1991, TA operated primarily as a sales company within Olivetti; it later changed ownership and has belonged to Kyocera since 2010.
family.triumph-adler-dario.description: The Dario desktop family preserves Triumph-Adler's branded versions of the compact Olivetti-era 80286 and 80386SX platforms. BluMach gives them independent machine identities while sharing verified board behavior with their PCS equivalents.
product.ta-dario286.summary: Documented 12 MHz 80286 desktop, equivalent to the Olivetti PCS 286
product.ta-dario286.history: Triumph-Adler marketed this TA-built platform as Dario 286 and P35 while the same motherboard was sold under the Olivetti PCS 286 name. The exceptionally detailed June 1990 technical training manual identifies the actual board assemblies, chip set, clocks, memory population, jumpers, CMOS layout and service diagnostics.
product.ta-dario286.technical.cpu_bus: Intel 80286 at 12 MHz with one wait state; Extended Setup F7 switches memory and I/O operation between 12 and 6 MHz. An Intel 80287 is optional.
product.ta-dario286.technical.chipset: The service manual identifies the G2 GC101A and GC102 controller pair plus the proprietary IOC. BluMach uses the GC10x core with the proven PCS 286 IOC02 behavior.
product.ta-dario286.technical.memory: CSAA03/06/09 board variants and SIMM combinations provide 512 KB, 640 KB, 1 MB, 2 MB or 4 MB. The standard 1 MB arrangement is 512 KB soldered plus two 256 KB SIMMs.
product.ta-dario286.technical.storage: WD37C65B floppy control and IDE disks. Documented factory drives include Conner CP3022/CP3024 20 MB and CP346/CP3044 40 MB models.
product.ta-dario286.technical.jumpers: A11 enables or disables the password; B07/B08 select DD or HD floppy operation; X04 selects the SIMM or system-board memory bank.
product.ta-dario286.technical.cmos: The DS1287 exposes 128 CMOS bytes. The manual documents floppy at 10h, disk at 12h/19h/1Ah, equipment at 14h, memory at 15h–18h and 30h–31h, language at 1Bh, video at 1Ch, password at 37h–3Fh and checksums at 2Eh/2Fh and 7Eh/7Fh.
product.ta-dario286.technical.diagnostic: Resident Diagnostics run at boot. Customer Test is supplied on CSFA12 and started with CUSTOMER; its floppy test writes to disk number 1.
product.ta-dario286.technical.identity: The Dario and PCS 286 are the same TA-built platform. In the absence of a separately labelled Dario dump, BluMach deliberately uses the preserved PCS 286 BIOS 1.37/1.42 set rather than inventing firmware differences.
product.ta-dario286.technical.verified: Shares the booted PCS 286 implementation: BIOS 1.42, Setup, Resident Diagnostics, MS-DOS, GC101/102 memory-control test and 20/40 MB IDE configurations.
product.ta-dario286.technical.limitation: The original keyboard-controller firmware is not preserved and is represented by the Olivetti-compatible KBC behavior. A Dario-labelled BIOS dump would still be valuable for archival comparison.
product.ta-dario286.document.technical: TA Dario 286 technical training manual DK000.00000.BA025, June 1990, 46 pages
product.ta-dario286.document.user: TA Dario 286 installation and operating manual (German)
product.ta-dario286.document.illustratio: Illustration supplement to the TA Dario 286 installation and operating manual
product.ta-dario286.document.components: Combined component data sheets referenced by the preserved Dario 286 board documentation
product.ta-dario286.document.wd90c00: Western Digital WD90C00 VGA controller data sheet
product.ta-dario286.document.tl16c451: Texas Instruments TL16C451 UART and parallel-port data sheet
product.ta-dario286.document.ld1107: Silicon Logic LD1107/VL16C451 UART and parallel-port data sheet
product.ta-dario386sx.summary: Triumph-Adler badge of the 16 MHz PCS 386SX platform, with preserved original ROMs
product.ta-dario386sx.history: Triumph-Adler sold the 80386SX member of this common platform as Dario 386SX or P45. Comparison of surviving version 1.14 ROMs proves that its executable video and system firmware is identical to the Olivetti PCS 386SX; only unused EPROM padding differs.
product.ta-dario386sx.technical.identity: Offsets 00000h–05FFFh (OVC 1.06) and 10000h–1FFFFh (Phoenix 1.14) are byte-identical to PCS 386SX. All 40,959 differing bytes lie in unused 06000h–0FFFFh padding: mostly FFh on Dario and 00h on Olivetti.
product.ta-dario386sx.technical.rom_layo: Original 64 KB LOW and HIGH dumps interleave exactly into the 128 KB FULL image. BluMach loads the Dario originals, preserving their FFh erased-area state rather than normalizing it to the Olivetti image.
product.ta-dario386sx.technical.bios_rev: Phoenix system BIOS 1.14 dated 30 October 1991 with 24 KB OVC video BIOS 1.06, Resident Diagnostics and tables.
product.ta-dario386sx.technical.chipset: Shares the PCS 386SX model: Headland HT18-B memory/EMS/shadow control, IOC02, PC87310 I/O and integrated PVGA1A. Exact physical board revisions remain a research target.
product.ta-dario386sx.technical.verified: ROM reconstruction and executable identity are proven; the shared implementation boots BIOS, Built-In Setup and MS-DOS with configured memory and IDE disks.
product.ta-dario386sx.technical.limitati: Like the PCS 386SX, this machine remains experimental while the complete chipset map, some CMOS/POST details and the Customer Utility U_MGR hang are investigated.
product.ta-dario386sx.document.ht18: Headland HT18 80386SX Single Chip manual, revision 2, September 1991
product.ta-dario386sx.document.olivetti: Olivetti PCS 386SX product sheet for the badge-equivalent platform
product.ta-dario386sx.document.firmware: Preserved TA Dario and Olivetti PCS 386SX version 1.14 LOW/HIGH/FULL dumps and byte-level comparison
